tech_name: Virtual cell foundation models (perturbation-response transformers)
principle: Train a sequence/expression model on millions of single cells whose state was measured after a defined genetic, chemical or cytokine perturbation, so that the transcriptomic consequence of knocking out or drugging a candidate target can be predicted in silico across cell contexts before any wet experiment is run; the target list is then triaged on predicted disease-relevant state shift rather than on literature enrichment.
trl_basis: Model published with public weights and a public benchmark challenge exists, but no target nominated by a virtual cell model has been shown to survive a human efficacy readout; that is proof of concept, not validation in a relevant environment. [E-8005][E-8008]
developers: Arc Institute; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub; Tahoe Therapeutics; NVIDIA BioNeMo; academic labs contributing to Virtual Cell Challenge
decisive_milestone: A target nominated prospectively by a virtual cell model, with no prior human genetic support and no prior literature, reaches Phase 2 and shows a target-engagement-linked efficacy signal; checkable by 2031 via ClinicalTrials.gov plus the sponsor's stated discovery provenance.
remaining_hard_problems: Training data are dominated by immortalised cancer cell lines under acute perturbation; the models predict mean expression shift, not disease phenotype, and there is no causal identifiability from observational transcriptomes. Generalisation to unseen genes and to primary diseased human tissue is unproven.
commercialization_reasoning: Requires (a) perturbation data in primary human diseased tissue, which the announced 2026 datasets do not provide, and (b) at least one full clinical cycle to test a model-nominated target; the earliest clinical readout that could count is therefore end of decade, and broad commercial reliance one clinical generation later.
failure_scenario: Models plateau at interpolating perturbations similar to their training distribution, are excellent at reproducing held-out cell lines and useless on novel biology, and settle into a permanent role as assay-triage tooling that never changes a go/no-go decision.
modality_scope: all modalities; strongest for small molecule and biologics target selection
notes: also relevant to B10 (it is a consumer of perturbation data)

tech_name: Human-genetics-anchored target selection (GWAS + colocalisation + Mendelian randomisation + ML integration)
principle: Use naturally occurring human genetic variation that alters a candidate target's function as a lifelong randomised experiment in humans, and select only targets where variant-phenotype direction matches the intended therapeutic direction; this substitutes human causal evidence for animal-model causal evidence at the point of target choice.
trl_basis: Routinely used in operations by multiple large sponsors through Open Targets and internal genetics units, with retrospective outcome analyses published; not 9 because no prospective, pre-registered demonstration of the effect size exists. [E-8009][E-8010]
developers: Open Targets (EMBL-EBI, Wellcome Sanger Institute, GSK, Genentech, MSD); Regeneron Genetics Center; deCODE genetics; UK Biobank; FinnGen
decisive_milestone: A pre-registered prospective cohort of targets selected after 2020, split by genetic support, reports differential Phase 2 to Phase 3 progression with the analysis plan published before readout; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Only a minority of biologically interesting targets have a tractable common-variant signal. Mendelian randomisation significance alone does not enrich for Phase 2 success. Tissue-specific eQTL attribution and horizontal pleiotropy remain unresolved, and the direction-of-effect inference frequently fails for targets whose biology is dose- and context-dependent.
commercialization_reasoning: Already commercially deployed; the range marks the period from Open Targets launch to present routine use rather than a future window.
failure_scenario: The reported approximate doubling of approval odds turns out to be partly a selection artefact: genetically supported targets cluster in indications with objective biomarkers and short trials, so the apparent probability gain does not transfer to indications where attrition actually concentrates.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: the single highest-elasticity bottleneck (B1, elasticity point 10) and the only mature technology attacking it

tech_name: In vivo spatially resolved pooled CRISPR screening (Perturb-DBiT, Perturb-Multimodal)
principle: Deliver a large sgRNA library into intact tissue, then read out perturbation identity and spatial whole-transcriptome response on the same tissue section, so that gene function is measured in the native microenvironment including stroma and immune contact rather than in dissociated monoculture.
trl_basis: Peer-reviewed platform papers in Nature Biotechnology and Cell demonstrating 80,000-guide panels in tissue sections; component validation in a laboratory setting, not yet a validated discovery pipeline. [E-8011][E-8012]
developers: Yale University (Rong Fan laboratory); Broad Institute; Whitehead Institute (Weissman laboratory); Arc Institute
decisive_milestone: A therapeutic target first nominated by an in vivo spatial perturbation screen, in human or humanised tissue, reaches IND; checkable by 2032 from the sponsor's published discovery narrative.
remaining_hard_problems: Library delivery into human-relevant tissue is the actual constraint; sgRNA capture efficiency in spatial assays is low, and the mouse tumour or mouse organ in which the screen runs re-imports the very animal-model predictivity problem the approach was meant to bypass.
commercialization_reasoning: Platform papers appeared 2025-2026; historical lag from a published screening modality to first IND traceable to it has been roughly five to eight years for pooled CRISPR generally, and delivery into human tissue is unsolved.
failure_scenario: The readout stays a transcriptomic proxy. Screens produce long ranked lists that reproduce known biology, and the spatial dimension adds cost without changing which target is picked.
modality_scope: all modalities; primarily oncology and immunology target discovery

tech_name: Genome-scale Perturb-seq in primary human cells
principle: Run pooled CRISPR perturbation with single-cell transcriptomic readout directly in primary human immune or tissue cells from donors, rather than in immortalised lines, so that the regulatory network measured is the one that exists in human physiology.
trl_basis: Genome-scale Perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells and pooled knockout screens in primary human myeloid cells are published; the method is validated in a relevant biological environment but not yet a routine, costed service. [E-8087]
developers: University of California San Francisco (Marson laboratory); Broad Institute; Whitehead Institute (Weissman laboratory); commercial single-cell providers
decisive_milestone: A commercial or core-facility service offers genome-scale Perturb-seq in primary patient-derived cells at a published price under roughly USD 500,000 per screen with donor replication; checkable by 2030 from provider price lists.
remaining_hard_problems: Editing efficiency and viability in primary cells vary sharply by donor and cell type; donor-to-donor variance can exceed the perturbation effect; cost per screen is currently prohibitive for anything but flagship programmes.
commercialization_reasoning: The method exists now in leading academic laboratories; commoditisation historically follows two to five years behind for single-cell methods, gated mainly by reagent cost curves.
failure_scenario: Donor heterogeneity swamps perturbation signal, forcing screens back to pooled donors or cell lines and reintroducing the artificiality the method was meant to remove.
modality_scope: biologics and cell therapy target discovery; immunology-weighted

tech_name: Chemical-genetic perturbation atlases as an industrial data factory (Tahoe Mosaic-class)
principle: Industrialise the generation side rather than the model side: run tens of thousands of drug and cytokine perturbations across dozens of cell models at single-cell resolution and release the atlas, so that mechanism-of-action and target deconvolution can be done by nearest-neighbour lookup against a dense reference rather than by bespoke experiments.
trl_basis: Tahoe-100M was produced, released and widely redistributed, and a four-fold larger successor was announced in January 2026; the platform demonstrably operates at industrial scale, but its output has not yet been shown to change a target decision. [E-8006][E-8007]
developers: Tahoe Therapeutics; Arc Institute; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub
decisive_milestone: A published case in which a first-in-class target or a mechanism-of-action reassignment derived solely from atlas lookup is confirmed by an orthogonal wet experiment and carried into a development programme; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Fifty cancer cell lines are not human tissue diversity; single-dose or three-dose exposure is not pharmacology; and the transcriptome is a proxy for phenotype that fails precisely for targets acting post-transcriptionally.
commercialization_reasoning: The data already exist and are already being sold and licensed; the commercial question is whether decision value follows, which the announced 2026 expansion should settle within a few years.
failure_scenario: The atlas becomes a benchmark artefact: heavily downloaded, heavily cited, and used almost entirely to train and compare models rather than to make discovery decisions.
modality_scope: small molecule mechanism-of-action; oncology-weighted
notes: primary data resource; also underpins B10

tech_name: Cross-tissue 3D spatial human reference atlases (Human Cell Atlas, HuBMAP)
principle: Build a spatially resolved, donor-diverse reference of which cell types express which genes in which anatomical context, so that a candidate target's expression footprint - and therefore its on-target off-tissue liability and its cell-type-specific rationale - can be checked against real human tissue rather than bulk GTEx averages.
trl_basis: Large parts of the atlas are released and in operational research use, but the 2026 consortium agenda still lists a clinically applicable 3D cross-tissue reference as work in progress, so the resource is not yet complete or decision-grade. [E-8013]
developers: Human Cell Atlas consortium; HuBMAP; Wellcome Sanger Institute; Broad Institute; Vizgen and 10x Genomics as platform vendors
decisive_milestone: An IND or briefing package in which atlas-derived cell-type-specific expression is cited as the basis for an on-target safety argument and the agency does not require a supplementary animal tissue cross-reactivity study; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Sampling is biased toward accessible tissues and toward donors who die in ways that permit collection; diseased-tissue coverage lags healthy coverage; and expression presence is not causal involvement.
commercialization_reasoning: Atlas completion targets are consortium-declared rather than contractual, and regulatory reliance on an atlas requires a qualification-style precedent that does not yet exist.
failure_scenario: The atlas is descriptively magnificent and decisionally inert: it tells you where a gene is expressed, which was rarely the reason a target failed.
modality_scope: all modalities

tech_name: Liver microphysiological systems for drug-induced liver injury inside the FDA ISTAND pathway
principle: Perfuse primary human hepatocytes with non-parenchymal cells in a flow device that reproduces sinusoidal shear and zonation, and read out multiple hepatic injury markers simultaneously, so that human-specific hepatotoxicity invisible to rodents is detected before first-in-human dosing.
trl_basis: A letter of intent was accepted into ISTAND in September 2024, which is step one of three in drug development tool qualification; the technology is demonstrated in a relevant environment but is not qualified and is not routinely accepted third-party evidence. [E-8003][E-8030]
developers: Emulate; CN Bio Innovations; Javelin Biotech; 3Rs Collaborative; FDA CDER; Liver Chip academic groups
decisive_milestone: FDA issues a qualification decision for a liver MPS with a stated context of use, and at least one sponsor cites that qualification in a submission without a parallel animal hepatotoxicity study; checkable by 2031 on the FDA DDT qualification programme page.
remaining_hard_problems: Idiosyncratic DILI is immune-mediated and most chips contain no adaptive immune compartment. Reported sensitivity of the best-characterised human liver models is around 69 percent at full specificity, so roughly a third of hepatotoxins are still missed. Inter-laboratory reproducibility and hepatocyte donor variability remain unquantified at qualification standard.
commercialization_reasoning: ISTAND letters of intent historically take several years to reach a qualification decision; the March 2026 NAM draft guidance supplies the missing evaluative framework, so a decision in the late 2020s is plausible and industry uptake follows one to three years after.
failure_scenario: Qualification arrives with a context of use so narrow - one injury mechanism, one compound class - that sponsors run the chip and the rodent study, adding cost and removing none.
modality_scope: small molecule primarily; biologics hepatotoxicity is rarely the failure mode
notes: also serves B8

tech_name: Multi-organ body-on-chip with linked pharmacokinetic scaling
principle: Fluidically connect liver, kidney, heart, gut and other tissue chips at physiologically scaled volumes and flow ratios so that a compound's metabolites - not just the parent compound - reach downstream organs, allowing human ADME-toxicity interactions to be observed in vitro.
trl_basis: Multi-organ systems are published and commercially available as research instruments, but no regulatory submission has substituted one for a required repeat-dose toxicology study; component validation only. [E-8001][E-8095]
developers: Emulate; CN Bio Innovations; Hesperos; TissUse; NIH NCATS Tissue Chip programme; Wyss Institute
decisive_milestone: A sponsor's IND is cleared where a 28-day repeat-dose systemic toxicity conclusion rests on a multi-organ MPS package and no corresponding rodent study is submitted; checkable by 2033.
remaining_hard_problems: There is no agreed allometric scaling law between chip compartments; a single shared medium cannot simultaneously satisfy each tissue's requirements; and the systems lack immune, neuroendocrine and microbiome axes that drive much systemic toxicity.
commercialization_reasoning: Single-organ chips have taken roughly a decade to reach the first step of qualification; a multi-organ system must clear the single-organ precedent first and then solve scaling, so it trails by at least one regulatory generation.
failure_scenario: Complexity outruns characterisation: each added organ adds failure modes and variance faster than it adds predictive signal, and the field consolidates back onto well-characterised single-organ chips.
modality_scope: small molecule; ADC payload systemic toxicity
notes: depends on single-organ MPS qualification (T-007) being established first

tech_name: Patient-derived organoid co-clinical response prediction
principle: Expand a patient's own tumour or tissue as a self-organising 3D culture that retains its genetic and architectural features, expose it to the candidate therapy, and use the ex vivo response as a predictor of that patient's clinical response - converting the animal-model predictivity question into a human-tissue measurement.
trl_basis: Retrospective concordance is published with positive predictive value around 0.78 and negative predictive value around 0.80, and prospective co-clinical trials are registered and running; validated in a relevant environment but not yet in an interventional randomised setting. [E-8083]
developers: Hubrecht Institute (Clevers laboratory); academic organoid biobanks; Crown Bioscience; Xilis; multiple hospital-based co-clinical programmes
decisive_milestone: A prospective randomised trial in which organoid-guided therapy selection beats physician-choice standard of care on progression-free survival reports a positive result; checkable by 2031 on ClinicalTrials.gov.
remaining_hard_problems: Organoids drop the stroma, vasculature and immune compartment that determine much of real drug response; establishment success rates are poor for several tumour types; and the two-to-six-week turnaround is longer than the clinical decision window in aggressive disease.
commercialization_reasoning: Prospective co-clinical trials are enrolling now and read out in the late 2020s; reimbursement as a companion diagnostic would follow a positive interventional result by two to four years.
failure_scenario: Organoids predict chemotherapy sensitivity - which was already predictable - and fail exactly where prediction is needed, on immunotherapy and on stroma-dependent agents, so the technology is confined to a shrinking slice of oncology.
modality_scope: oncology small molecule and ADC; limited applicability to systemic biologics

tech_name: Immune-competent organoids and lymphoid organoid systems
principle: Reconstruct a functioning human adaptive immune compartment in vitro - tumour organoids co-cultured with autologous lymphocytes, or organoids grown from lymphoid tissue - so that immune-mediated efficacy and immune-mediated toxicity, the two failure modes least served by animal models, can be measured in human cells.
trl_basis: Engineered human immune organoids are described in review literature as an emerging research capability; no standardised, reproducible platform with published predictive performance exists. [E-8084]
developers: Academic translational immunology groups; Stanford and MIT tissue engineering laboratories; early-stage companies commercialising lymphoid organoids
decisive_milestone: A published head-to-head study in which an immune organoid platform prospectively predicts clinical response or cytokine release syndrome for a T-cell engager or checkpoint agent across at least twenty compounds; checkable by 2032.
remaining_hard_problems: Germinal centre formation, antigen presentation timing and lymphocyte trafficking cannot yet be sustained in vitro for the weeks that adaptive responses require; autologous immune cells from patients are limited and heterogeneous.
commercialization_reasoning: The core immunological problem - sustaining adaptive immunity ex vivo - has resisted solution for decades and there is no announced programme with a near-term milestone; commercial availability therefore sits beyond 2030.
failure_scenario: The systems reproduce innate activation convincingly and adaptive memory not at all, so they predict acute cytokine release but not durable efficacy, which is the question sponsors actually need answered.
modality_scope: cell therapy, T-cell engagers, checkpoint inhibitors, vaccines
notes: one of the few technologies aimed squarely at immune-mediated attrition; low TRL

tech_name: Humanised-immune-system mice (HIS mice, HLA-transgenic models)
principle: Engraft human haematopoietic stem cells or PBMCs into immunodeficient mice, optionally with human HLA transgenes, so that a human immune system - rather than a mouse one - reacts to a human-targeted biologic in a whole-organism setting.
trl_basis: Available as a routine catalogue service from multiple contract research organisations and used in IND-enabling packages, which is operational-environment demonstration; not 9 because no regulatory qualification exists and agencies do not accept these data as a substitute for required studies. [E-8085]
developers: The Jackson Laboratory; Taconic Biosciences; Crown Bioscience; genOway; academic humanised-mouse cores
decisive_milestone: A regulator accepts HIS-mouse cytokine release or immunogenicity data in place of a non-human primate study for a T-cell engager or CAR construct in a cleared IND; checkable by 2030 from published regulatory precedent or sponsor disclosure.
remaining_hard_problems: Human myeloid and complement reconstitution is incomplete in most models; human T cells are educated on mouse thymic epithelium in the common models, distorting the repertoire; graft-versus-host disease limits study duration.
commercialization_reasoning: Already commercially available; the range describes existing operational use, and the open question is regulatory acceptance rather than technical availability.
failure_scenario: The models overpredict cytokine release for some constructs and underpredict for others without a rule that distinguishes the two, so agencies continue to require the primate study and the mouse work becomes an additional cost line.
modality_scope: biologics, T-cell engagers, cell therapy, vaccines
notes: high TRL but regulatory acceptance, not technology, is the binding constraint - depends on B5

tech_name: NAM regulatory acceptance framework as an institutional technology (FDA NAM guidance, animal-testing roadmap, FDA Modernization Act 3.0)
principle: Change the evidentiary rule rather than the assay: define context of use, human biological relevance, technical characterisation and fit-for-purpose as the four axes on which a non-animal method is judged, and remove statutory language that can be read as mandating animal data, so that a sponsor can rationally invest in human-relevant methods.
trl_basis: Draft guidance issued March 2026, an agency roadmap published April 2025, and statutory reform passed both chambers; the framework is demonstrated in a relevant setting but no product has been approved on a NAM-only nonclinical package. [E-8001][E-8002][E-8004]
developers: FDA CDER and CBER; U.S. Congress; NIH NCATS; EU Reference Laboratory for alternatives to animal testing; Animal Wellness Action and allied advocacy coalitions
decisive_milestone: A new molecular entity is approved where at least one pivotal nonclinical safety conclusion rests on NAM data with no corresponding animal study in the submission; checkable by 2032 from the approval package review documents.
remaining_hard_problems: There is no validated human reference outcome set against which NAMs can be benchmarked - the historical animal data were never validated against human outcomes either, so the field lacks a ground truth to calibrate against. Liability and precedent conservatism mean sponsors will run the animal study regardless until a first mover survives.
commercialization_reasoning: Guidance is in draft now; final guidance typically follows one to three years, and first sponsor reliance follows the first precedent, which requires a sponsor willing to absorb the review risk.
failure_scenario: The framework is adopted in form and ignored in practice: sponsors submit NAM data as supportive alongside a complete conventional package, so nonclinical cost rises and no timeline shortens.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: institutional rather than laboratory technology; rated on the TRL analogue scale

tech_name: LLM-based EHR prescreening and trial matching (TRIAGE-class systems)
principle: Parse unstructured clinical notes, pathology and genomic reports against a protocol's eligibility criteria and return a cited eligibility determination, so that the chart-review step performed by clinical research coordinators is done in seconds instead of hours.
trl_basis: Validated against multi-year health-system EHR data and published in a peer-reviewed clinical informatics journal, and deployed in operational prescreening workflows; not higher because a randomised evaluation found accuracy gains without efficiency gains. [E-8034][E-8035]
developers: Academic medical centre informatics groups; Mayo Clinic and Memorial Sloan Kettering research informatics; Trially; Deep 6 AI; Paradigm; large EHR vendors
decisive_milestone: A multi-site prospective randomised comparison reports shortened time from protocol activation to last-patient-in, not merely improved chart-abstraction accuracy; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: The randomised evidence to date shows the tool improves accuracy while leaving throughput unchanged, which indicates the binding constraint is elsewhere - site staff availability, physician referral behaviour and patient willingness. Criteria written in prose that clinicians themselves interpret inconsistently cannot be resolved by better parsing.
commercialization_reasoning: Already commercially deployed; the window reflects the period over which enterprise adoption completes, not a technical milestone.
failure_scenario: The technology works exactly as advertised and total enrollment does not move, because chart review was never the rate-limiting step; sponsors pay for prescreening software and enrollment timelines stay flat.
modality_scope: all modalities; oncology-weighted deployment
notes: LOW-VALUE FLAG: strong candidate for making an already-fast step faster; randomised data show no efficiency gain [E-8035], and 59 percent of sites lose patients before screening [E-8091]

tech_name: Registry-based and embedded pragmatic randomised trials
principle: Randomise inside an existing disease or procedure registry that already captures the outcome of interest, so that consent, randomisation and follow-up ride on infrastructure that exists for clinical care, eliminating dedicated case report forms, monitoring visits and separate follow-up.
trl_basis: Executed at scale in real regulatory-relevant settings - TASTE and STRESS are completed trials with published economics showing registry designs at roughly a third of explanatory trial cost; proven in operations for specific settings. [E-8038][E-8092]
developers: Uppsala Clinical Research Center and SWEDEHEART; Duke Clinical Research Institute; NIH Collaboratory; national cardiovascular and transplant registries; FDA and EMA methods groups
decisive_milestone: A registry-based randomised trial serves as the primary evidence for a US or EU label expansion of a new molecular entity, not merely a comparative-effectiveness question for approved products; checkable by 2030 from approval documents.
remaining_hard_problems: Registry endpoints are collected for care, not for regulatory adjudication - definitions drift, adjudication is absent, and blinding is usually impossible. The design only exists where a comprehensive national registry exists, which excludes most of the US and most disease areas.
commercialization_reasoning: Already in operation since the TASTE trial; the constraint is the availability of registries with regulatory-grade endpoint capture, not technology maturity.
failure_scenario: The cost advantage collapses once a regulator demands source-data verification and independent endpoint adjudication, at which point the registry trial converges on conventional trial cost and loses its only advantage.
modality_scope: small molecule and device-adjacent; cardiovascular, transplant, critical care
notes: depends on endpoint measurability (B15)

tech_name: Decentralised and hybrid trial operations (home nursing, direct-to-patient supply, televisits)
principle: Move assessments and drug delivery to the participant's home and keep only what genuinely requires a clinic at the site, removing travel burden as a reason for non-participation and non-retention, and widening the geographic catchment beyond academic centres.
trl_basis: Widely deployed as hybrid elements and supported by vendor networks, but only about 6 percent of the decentralised-trial literature contains empirical performance data and roughly 1 percent of industry trial starts used decentralised solutions in the assessed period, so operational demonstration is real but thin. [E-8036][E-8037]
developers: IQVIA; Fortrea and other clinical research organisations; Science 37; Medable; home health nursing networks; sponsors running hybrid designs
decisive_milestone: A preregistered head-to-head comparison of a decentralised and a conventional arm of the same protocol reports enrollment rate and 12-month retention with the analysis plan published in advance; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: The published performance claims come from sponsor-selected matched comparisons whose matching methodology is not disclosed, so the effect size is not independently establishable. Home assessment introduces measurement heterogeneity that some endpoints cannot absorb, and investigator oversight obligations under GCP were written for site-based conduct.
commercialization_reasoning: Deployment is already underway; the window covers the period to routine hybrid default, gated by ICH E6(R3) Annex 2 finalisation rather than by any technical development.
failure_scenario: Decentralisation shifts burden from the participant to the site coordinator, who is the actually scarce resource; sites decline decentralised protocols, and adoption stalls at the elements sponsors can run without site cooperation.
modality_scope: all modalities; chronic disease and rare disease strongest

tech_name: Federated real-world data networks for feasibility and site selection
principle: Query harmonised EHR and claims data across many health systems without moving patient-level data, to count how many eligible patients actually exist at each candidate site before the protocol is finalised, replacing site-reported feasibility estimates that systematically overpromise.
trl_basis: Commercial federated networks are in routine third-party operational use for feasibility and cohort discovery; not 9 because outcome evidence that network-informed site selection reduces non-enrolling sites is vendor-reported rather than independent. [E-8036][E-8049]
developers: TriNetX; Aetion; Datavant; OHDSI/OMOP community; national health data spaces in the EU
decisive_milestone: An independent published analysis shows that sponsors using federated feasibility data have a non-enrolling-site share below 10 percent, against a conventional baseline above 20 percent, across at least 50 trials; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Coded EHR data undercount the eligibility criteria that actually drive screen failure - performance status, prior line of therapy, washout - so counts of apparently eligible patients overstate the enrollable pool. Data recency and coverage vary by network member.
commercialization_reasoning: Already commercial and widely licensed; the remaining question is measured benefit, not availability.
failure_scenario: Feasibility counts improve while enrollment does not, because the constraint was the site's staffed capacity to run one more protocol rather than the existence of patients.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: Milestone quantified per X-25.

tech_name: Master protocols: basket, umbrella and platform trials with shared controls
principle: Run one overarching protocol with a common control arm and shared infrastructure across many sub-populations or many candidate agents, so that each additional question costs an increment rather than a whole trial, and control patients are reused instead of re-randomised for each programme.
trl_basis: Executed at scale in oncology and infectious disease for a decade, with FDA issuing revised draft guidance on master protocols; proven in operations, not 9 because platform designs remain rare outside oncology and pandemic settings. [E-8041]
developers: National Cancer Institute (NCI-MATCH lineage); Friends of Cancer Research; Berry Consultants; UK RECOVERY investigators; EU-PEARL
decisive_milestone: A platform trial outside oncology and outside pandemic infectious disease supports a first approval in a chronic disease indication; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Shared control arms require agreement among competing sponsors on standard of care, data access and publication, which is a governance problem, not a statistical one. Long-running platforms suffer drift in standard of care that undermines comparability across cohorts entered years apart.
commercialization_reasoning: Already operational; the expansion question is governance and sponsor willingness rather than method readiness.
failure_scenario: Sponsors decline to place assets in a shared platform because the comparative readout is unflattering and uncontrollable, so platforms persist only where a public funder pays for them.
modality_scope: all modalities; oncology, infectious disease, neurology

tech_name: Bayesian information borrowing and external control arms
principle: Formally borrow strength across related sub-populations or from external data sources through a hierarchical prior calibrated so that borrowing shrinks when the sources disagree, so that a trial in a fragmented population needs fewer newly randomised patients to reach a defensible conclusion.
trl_basis: FDA issued a 2026 draft guidance on Bayesian methods and a revised master protocol draft guidance; methods are validated in simulation and used in specific accepted submissions, but the guidance is draft and general acceptance is not established. [E-8041]
developers: FDA CDER Office of Biostatistics; Berry Consultants; academic biostatistics groups; EMA methodology working parties; sponsors of rare disease programmes
decisive_milestone: A pivotal approval where the primary analysis prespecifies Bayesian borrowing from an external control and the agency accepts it without requiring a concurrent randomised comparison; checkable by 2030 from approval review documents.
remaining_hard_problems: Borrowing is only valid when the external population is exchangeable with the trial population, and exchangeability cannot be verified from the data being borrowed. Operating characteristics degrade sharply under unmeasured confounding, and type I error inflation under prior-data conflict is design-specific rather than generic.
commercialization_reasoning: Draft guidance now, finalisation typically one to three years, and precedent-setting approvals follow; the sequence puts routine acceptance around the turn of the decade.
failure_scenario: Agencies accept borrowing only in settings where a randomised trial was infeasible anyway, so the method never reduces the size of the trials that dominate development cost.
modality_scope: rare disease, oncology, gene therapy

tech_name: Population genomic newborn screening to build trial-ready rare disease cohorts
principle: Sequence newborns against a panel of actionable early-onset conditions so that patients are identified pre-symptomatically and in known numbers, converting a scattered, late-diagnosed, heterogeneous population into an identified cohort that can be approached before irreversible pathology accrues.
trl_basis: GUARDIAN has sequenced over 13,000 newborns against 460+ conditions with published first results, and the Generation Study targets 100,000 genomes; validated in a relevant environment at research scale, not implemented as standard care. [E-8043][E-8044]
developers: GeneDx and Columbia University (GUARDIAN); Genomics England and NHS England (Generation Study); state newborn screening programmes; BeginNGS consortium
decisive_milestone: A therapeutic trial enrolls a majority of its participants from a genomic newborn screening programme and reports a pre-symptomatic treatment benefit; checkable by 2032.
remaining_hard_problems: Penetrance for many screened variants is unknown, so pre-symptomatic identification generates patients who may never develop disease and cannot ethically be randomised to an intervention; consent frameworks for population sequencing of infants remain contested; and health systems have no pathway to fund follow-up for thousands of uncertain findings.
commercialization_reasoning: Research cohorts are enrolling now; transition to routine public health screening requires national policy decisions and cost-effectiveness evidence that will take most of a decade.
failure_scenario: Screening finds patients faster than therapies exist for them, generating a diagnosed-but-untreatable population and a political backlash that narrows the permitted panel back toward the conventional list.
modality_scope: gene therapy, ASO, enzyme replacement; rare disease only
notes: the only technology in this catalogue that increases the identified patient pool rather than reallocating it

tech_name: Individualised n-of-1 antisense oligonucleotide pathway with a regulatory platform template
principle: Treat the chemistry class as the regulated platform and the specific sequence as a variable, with FDA guidance defining a reduced, standardised IND package for a product intended for one or two individuals, so that ultra-fragmented populations become addressable without a conventional development programme per patient.
trl_basis: FDA has issued both clinical and CMC guidance for individualised ASO INDs and multiple academic sponsor-investigator programmes operate under them; demonstrated in the operational regulatory environment, not 9 because there is no approved product and no reimbursement pathway. [E-8042]
developers: n-Lorem Foundation; Boston Children's Hospital (Yu laboratory); FDA CDER; Ionis Pharmaceuticals; academic sponsor-investigator networks
decisive_milestone: A sustainable funding and reimbursement mechanism carries at least fifty individualised ASO treatments per year in the US with published outcome tracking; checkable by 2031 from programme reports.
remaining_hard_problems: There is no way to establish efficacy in a single patient without a validated within-patient biomarker, so most treatments remain uninterpretable. Long-term safety of bespoke sequences cannot be characterised. The CMC burden per patient does not fall with volume because each sequence is a new product.
commercialization_reasoning: The regulatory pathway exists now; the binding constraint is philanthropic and payer funding, which determines whether volume grows past a few dozen patients per year.
failure_scenario: The model stays confined to charitably funded single-digit annual volumes because no payer will reimburse a therapy that cannot demonstrate efficacy, and it never becomes a general answer to population fragmentation.
modality_scope: antisense oligonucleotide; extendable in principle to siRNA and gene editing

tech_name: Agency-internal generative AI for review workflow (FDA Elsa and successors)
principle: Give reviewers a model that summarises submissions, compares labels, drafts adverse-event summaries and locates precedent, so that reviewer hours shift from document retrieval to scientific judgement and review capacity rises without headcount.
trl_basis: Deployed agency-wide ahead of schedule and in active use, but reported to produce incorrect safety outputs and irrelevant guidance requiring manual rework, so it is demonstrated in a relevant environment rather than proven in operations. [E-8045]
developers: FDA (Office of the Commissioner and CDER); federal cloud vendors; EMA and other agencies running parallel initiatives
decisive_milestone: FDA publishes review-cycle metrics showing a sustained reduction in median first-cycle review time or in review-related information requests attributable to AI tooling, with the measurement method disclosed; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Regulatory review is an accountability function: a reviewer must be able to defend a conclusion, and a model that is confidently wrong on safety data transfers verification burden rather than removing it. There is no accepted method for auditing a generative summary against a 100,000-page submission.
commercialization_reasoning: The tool is deployed now; the window is the time needed for verification workflows to mature enough that reviewers rely on outputs rather than re-checking them.
failure_scenario: Net reviewer time rises because every output must be independently verified, and the tool is quietly relegated to low-stakes administrative drafting.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: B5 elasticity point is 0.4, among the lowest in the matrix

tech_name: AI model credibility qualification framework (FDA seven-step, context-of-use based)
principle: Instead of qualifying a model as generically valid, define the specific regulatory question it answers, grade the consequence of the model being wrong, and require credibility evidence proportional to that risk, so that model-based evidence has a defined route into a submission.
trl_basis: The framework exists as January 2025 draft guidance and remained draft as of mid-2026; it explicitly excludes early discovery, so it is a validated concept in a relevant setting without operational precedent. [E-8047]
developers: FDA CDER and CBER; EMA; ICH; ASME V&V 40 community whose risk-based credibility logic it adapts
decisive_milestone: A drug approval in which a named computational model's output is part of the pivotal evidence and the review documents cite the credibility assessment plan; checkable by 2031 from approval packages.
remaining_hard_problems: The framework requires a credibility assessment plan agreed in advance, which presupposes the sponsor knows the model's context of use before doing the work; and there is no accepted standard for how much held-out validation constitutes sufficient credibility for a given risk grade.
commercialization_reasoning: Finalisation of a January 2025 draft typically lands within one to three years, and first precedent-setting use follows the finalised text.
failure_scenario: The framework is finalised and sponsors avoid it, because opening a model to formal credibility assessment invites review scrutiny that a conventional package does not attract; model evidence stays supportive and unreviewed.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: gates the regulatory value of nearly every AI technology in this catalogue

tech_name: Expedited-review instruments: Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, platform technology designation, priority review vouchers
principle: Ration a scarce reviewer-attention resource explicitly by issuing transferable or awarded entitlements to accelerated review, and let prior knowledge about a shared platform carry across products so that each subsequent product on the same platform requires less new review.
trl_basis: Priority review vouchers are a decade-old operating programme and platform technology designation is in force; the CNPV pilot is newly launched and unproven, so the class as a whole is demonstrated in the operational environment. [E-8046][E-8062]
developers: FDA Office of the Commissioner; U.S. Congress; sponsors and voucher purchasers; CBER for platform technology designation
decisive_milestone: Published data show that products reviewed under CNPV reached their action date a median of at least 120 days earlier than matched non-voucher products, with post-market safety label changes within two years no higher than the matched comparator group; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Accelerating one application consumes the same reviewer pool, so vouchers reallocate rather than expand capacity unless total reviewer headcount grows; and there is no published evidence that compressed review preserves detection of safety signals.
commercialization_reasoning: Voucher programmes are operating now, with the pediatric programme reauthorised to 2029 and the CNPV pilot running; the open question is measured effect, not availability.
failure_scenario: Vouchers move a few products forward and push everything else back, so total approvals per year are unchanged and the instrument becomes a transfer of value to voucher sellers rather than a capacity increase.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: zero-sum unless reviewer headcount grows: this is capacity reallocation, not capacity creation Milestone quantified per X-25.

tech_name: Machine-readable regulatory submissions built on structured study definitions
principle: Carry the protocol, schedule of activities and analysis definitions as structured data from authoring through to submission, so that a reviewer receives queryable objects rather than a PDF and consistency checks are automated rather than manual.
trl_basis: USDM v4 and CDISC 360i reference implementations exist and produce machine-readable JSON, but no regulator accepts a structured study definition as the submission of record; validated in a relevant environment only. [E-8081][E-8082]
developers: CDISC; TransCelerate BioPharma Digital Data Flow initiative; FDA and PMDA standards groups; eCTD vendors
decisive_milestone: A regulator accepts a structured study definition as the authoritative protocol representation in a marketing application, not merely as a supplementary file; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: The standard must represent the full space of adaptive and complex designs without becoming so permissive that it stops being machine-checkable; and legacy submissions in unstructured form will coexist for a decade, so reviewers must operate both workflows.
commercialization_reasoning: CDISC 360i Phase 2 specifications complete in 2026, followed by vendor implementation, sponsor migration and then regulatory acceptance; each stage historically runs multiple years in this standards domain.
failure_scenario: Sponsors generate the structured artefact as a by-product of the PDF they still write, so the structure is unreliable, reviewers do not trust it, and the standard becomes compliance overhead.
modality_scope: all modalities

tech_name: Cell-free enzymatic DNA (doggybone DNA) replacing plasmid DNA - SHARED INPUTS
principle: Amplify a linear covalently closed DNA construct enzymatically in vitro instead of growing it in bacteria, removing fermentation, bacterial backbone, antibiotic resistance genes and endotoxin from the critical starting material for every viral vector, mRNA and cell therapy product.
trl_basis: FDA Drug Master File acceptance reported in 2022 and a cell-free DNA GMP licence reported in 2025, with a benchtop kit commercialised through New England Biolabs in March 2026; proven in a commercial GMP operation, not 9 because no approved product yet uses it as its critical starting material. [E-8020][E-8021]
developers: Touchlight Genetics; New England Biolabs; Ansa Biotechnologies; 4basebio; contract manufacturers adopting cell-free DNA
decisive_milestone: A licensed advanced therapy or mRNA product is approved with enzymatically produced DNA named as the critical starting material in the approved CMC section; checkable by 2031 from approval documents.
remaining_hard_problems: Linear DNA behaves differently from supercoiled plasmid in transfection and in AAV packaging, so process re-optimisation is required per product; enzymatic amplification fidelity across long or repetitive constructs must be demonstrated at commercial scale; and comparability bridging for products already in clinic is a full regulatory exercise.
commercialization_reasoning: GMP supply exists now, so the gating factor is that a product must complete development using it; a programme starting today reaches approval in roughly five to seven years.
failure_scenario: Sponsors already in clinic will not undertake comparability bridging, so adoption is limited to new programmes and the installed plasmid base persists for a decade.
modality_scope: gene therapy, mRNA, cell therapy, DNA vaccines - shared input across all
notes: SUB-AREA: shared inputs (plasmid/starting material)

tech_name: Robotic gloveless isolator aseptic fill-finish with small-batch and on-demand filling - SHARED INPUTS
principle: Remove the human operator from the aseptic core entirely by using robots inside a sealed decontaminated isolator, which eliminates the dominant contamination vector, permits far smaller economically viable batch sizes, and allows rapid product changeover for the many small-volume products that now dominate pipelines.
trl_basis: Robotic isolator systems are installed and running commercially, and FDA has cited gloveless isolators as a way to streamline CMC development; demonstrated in the operational environment with capacity expansion underway. [E-8027]
developers: Cytiva, Syntegon, Vanrx/Cytiva SA25, IMA, Steriline as equipment suppliers; CordenPharma and other fill-finish CDMOs; FDA Emerging Technology Program
decisive_milestone: A CDMO publicly reports routine multi-product changeover within a single shift on a robotic isolator line supporting commercial supply of more than five distinct products; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Environmental monitoring and media-fill validation standards were written for human-operated cleanrooms and translate awkwardly to robotics; Annex 1 contamination control strategy expectations for robotic systems are still being interpreted; and highly potent or cell-based products need containment approaches that conflict with the sterility design.
commercialization_reasoning: Equipment is commercially available now and capacity investment is underway; the window reflects the time for installed base to reach a scale where small-batch filling stops being a scheduling bottleneck.
failure_scenario: Capital cost per line keeps the technology concentrated in a few large CDMOs, so small-volume products still queue behind large-volume campaigns and access does not improve.
modality_scope: all injectable modalities; especially cell and gene therapy, ADC, mRNA
notes: SUB-AREA: shared inputs (fill-finish)

tech_name: Stable AAV producer cell lines with high-cell-density perfusion - VIRAL VECTOR
principle: Integrate rep, cap, helper functions and the transgene into a suspension-adapted mammalian cell line so that AAV is produced by simple induction at high cell density under perfusion, eliminating the triple plasmid transfection whose reagent cost and batch variability dominate viral vector economics.
trl_basis: A peer-reviewed process reports 3- to 6-fold titre increases reaching about 1e12 genome copies per mL confirmed in bioreactor, and commercial platform cell lines are licensed to developers; demonstrated in the operational environment but no approved AAV product yet uses a stable producer line. [E-8022][E-8023]
developers: Cytiva (ELEVECTA); Ultragenyx; Pfizer and other sponsors with internal producer lines; Oxford Biomedica and other vector CDMOs
decisive_milestone: An approved AAV gene therapy is manufactured on a stable producer cell line process at commercial scale, disclosed in the approved CMC section; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Genetic stability of integrated rep and cap over the many generations needed for commercial scale is the core unsolved problem, since rep is cytostatic; each new transgene requires a new cell line and a new development cycle, which reverses the platform advantage; and full-versus-empty capsid ratio is not necessarily improved.
commercialization_reasoning: Processes are validated at bioreactor scale now, but a producer line must be built into a programme from IND onward and carried through approval, which is a five- to eight-year sequence.
failure_scenario: Per-transgene cell line development takes longer than the transient process it replaces, so sponsors use stable lines only for products that reach large commercial volume - which almost no gene therapy does.
modality_scope: AAV gene therapy
notes: SUB-AREA: viral vector. Modality spread noted by Agent G is real: this is a vector-specific lever with no read-across to mAb

tech_name: AAV process intensification: perfusion bioreaction with integrated continuous clarification - VIRAL VECTOR
principle: Run the production bioreactor in perfusion at high cell density and take harvest continuously into an integrated clarification train, so that product is removed from the degradative culture environment as it forms and the facility footprint per dose falls.
trl_basis: Perfusion AAV processes with integrated clarification are published and running at pilot and clinical-supply scale; validated in a relevant environment and entering operational use, but not established as a licensed commercial process. [E-8022]
developers: Academic and industrial bioprocess groups publishing in Frontiers in Bioengineering; Sartorius, Repligen and Cytiva as equipment suppliers; vector CDMOs
decisive_milestone: A vector CDMO publishes commercial-scale cost of goods per dose for a perfusion-plus-continuous-clarification AAV process that is at least half its batch process baseline; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: AAV is shear- and pH-sensitive and continuous handling extends residence time in suboptimal conditions; continuous clarification of a lysate containing host cell DNA and empty capsids is far harder than clarifying a secreted protein; and full-versus-empty separation remains a batch chromatography step that breaks continuity.
commercialization_reasoning: The unit operations exist; integration and validation of a continuous train under GMP typically takes three to five years from pilot demonstration to licensed process.
failure_scenario: Downstream full-versus-empty separation stays batch and stays the bottleneck, so upstream intensification produces more crude material that the purification train cannot absorb.
modality_scope: AAV and lentiviral gene therapy
notes: SUB-AREA: viral vector

tech_name: In vivo CAR-T: eliminating per-patient cell manufacturing entirely - AUTOLOGOUS CELL THERAPY
principle: Deliver the CAR construct to T cells inside the patient using a targeted lipid nanoparticle carrying mRNA or a receptor-retargeted lentiviral vector, so that there is no apheresis, no ex vivo expansion, no cryopreservation and no per-patient batch record - the product becomes a vial rather than a manufacturing campaign.
trl_basis: Multiple Phase 1 programmes are enrolling with both LNP-mRNA and lentiviral approaches, and one developer was acquired by a large pharmaceutical company; demonstrated in a relevant clinical environment with no efficacy or durability readout at pivotal scale. [E-8014][E-8015][E-8089]
developers: Capstan Therapeutics (Eli Lilly); Umoja Biopharma (with Bristol Myers Squibb); Interius BioTherapeutics; EsoBiotec (AstraZeneca); Orna Therapeutics; Kelonia
decisive_milestone: A randomised or single-arm pivotal trial of an in vivo CAR product reports response rates within range of approved autologous CAR-T in the same indication, with no manufacturing failures and no requirement for apheresis; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Achieving sufficient transduction of the right T cell subset in vivo without transducing off-target cells is unsolved at therapeutic dose; transient mRNA CARs may not persist long enough for durable remission while integrating vectors carry insertional risk without the ex vivo release testing that currently mitigates it; and cytokine release cannot be dose-titrated once the vector is administered.
commercialization_reasoning: Phase 1 data are emerging now; a first approval requires a pivotal trial plus review, which from current Phase 1 status is typically four to seven years.
failure_scenario: In vivo transduction efficiency in humans proves an order of magnitude below the mouse data, so the CAR cell dose achieved is subtherapeutic, and raising the vector dose triggers hepatotoxicity or complement activation.
modality_scope: autologous cell therapy, redirected to a delivery problem
notes: SUB-AREA: autologous cell therapy. DEPENDENCY: this technology converts a manufacturing bottleneck (B6) into a targeted-delivery bottleneck (B7) - it presupposes B7 is solved

tech_name: Sub-24-hour and next-day automated closed-system CAR-T manufacture - AUTOLOGOUS CELL THERAPY
principle: Skip prolonged ex vivo activation and expansion, transduce freshly isolated T cells and return them within a day or three inside a closed automated cassette, so that vein-to-vein time collapses, the product retains a stem-like memory phenotype, and manufacturing slots per cleanroom per year multiply.
trl_basis: A sub-24-hour platform has Phase I clinical validation with 23 of 25 patients achieving MRD-negative complete remission at day 14, and a 72-hour automated workflow is in Phase 1/2; demonstrated clinically but not yet supporting an approved product. [E-8024][E-8025]
developers: Gracell/AstraZeneca (FasT CAR); Lonza (Cocoon); Miltenyi Biotec (CliniMACS Prodigy); Galapagos (GLPF5101, ATALANTA-1); academic decentralised manufacturing programmes
decisive_milestone: A rapid-manufactured CAR-T product is approved with a labelled vein-to-vein time under one week and a manufacturing success rate above 95 percent; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Release testing - sterility in particular - has historically taken longer than the new manufacturing time, so the bottleneck moves to quality control; potency assays for a minimally expanded product are not established; and decentralised point-of-care manufacture raises comparability questions across sites that no regulator has fully answered.
commercialization_reasoning: Clinical validation exists now and multiple programmes are in Phase 1/2; approval of a rapid-manufactured product plausibly lands in the late 2020s.
failure_scenario: Rapid sterility testing is not qualified in time, so the product still waits days for release and the clinical advantage of speed evaporates while the cost advantage is offset by decentralisation overhead.
modality_scope: autologous CAR-T and TCR-T
notes: SUB-AREA: autologous cell therapy

tech_name: Integrated continuous bioprocessing with N-1 perfusion intensification - BULK API / mAb
principle: Hold the seed train at very high density under perfusion so the production bioreactor is inoculated 5- to 10-fold denser, shortening the production phase, and connect the bioreactor to continuous capture chromatography so product leaves the reactor as it forms rather than accumulating.
trl_basis: Intensified perfusion seed trains and perfusion-to-continuous-capture are running in commercial biomanufacturing, while fully end-to-end continuous drug substance has been shown only at pilot scale; the hybrid is operational, the full concept is not. [E-8026][E-8093]
developers: Amgen, Genentech and Sanofi process development groups; Merck KGaA and Cytiva as suppliers; IIT Delhi (Rathore group); FDA Emerging Technology Program
decisive_milestone: A regulator approves a licensed commercial mAb process that is continuous from bioreactor through polishing with no intermediate hold tanks; checkable by 2031 from approval documents.
remaining_hard_problems: Viral clearance validation assumes discrete batch boundaries, and defining a batch in a continuous process is a regulatory and quality question that has no settled answer; continuous polishing and viral inactivation lag continuous capture; and a continuous train has no recovery path from a mid-run deviation.
commercialization_reasoning: Hybrid intensification is deployed now; end-to-end continuity requires the batch-definition and viral-clearance questions to be resolved, which is a regulatory-science timeline rather than an engineering one.
failure_scenario: The industry concludes that intensified batch captures most of the economic benefit at a fraction of the regulatory risk, and end-to-end continuous never becomes standard - a conclusion already argued in the 2026 literature.
modality_scope: monoclonal antibody and recombinant protein bulk drug substance
notes: SUB-AREA: bulk API/mAb. Note: mAb manufacturing is the sub-area with the most spare capacity, so improvements here have the weakest system effect

tech_name: Digital twins, AI soft sensors and PAT for real-time release - BULK API / mAb
principle: Run a mechanistic-plus-data hybrid model of the process in parallel with the physical process, fed by inline spectroscopy, so that critical quality attributes are inferred continuously and release can be based on demonstrated process state rather than on end-of-batch testing.
trl_basis: Digital twins and AI soft sensors are described as accelerating technologies in current bioprocessing practice and are running in process development, but real-time release of a biologic on model-inferred quality attributes is not established practice; validated in a relevant environment. [E-8026][E-8093]
developers: Sartorius, Cytiva and Siemens as platform vendors; Amgen and Merck process analytics groups; NIIMBL projects; academic process systems engineering groups
decisive_milestone: A licensed biologic is released commercially on a real-time release testing strategy where a model-inferred attribute substitutes for a compendial release assay; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Model drift over a product's commercial life must be detected and managed under a change control regime designed for fixed processes; inline spectroscopy has poor sensitivity for the low-abundance attributes that matter most, such as aggregates and host cell protein; and validating a model whose predictions are correlated with, but not identical to, the assay it replaces requires an equivalence standard that does not exist.
commercialization_reasoning: Real-time release for small molecules took roughly fifteen years from PAT initiative to routine use; biologics attributes are harder to measure inline, so a later window is warranted.
failure_scenario: Regulators require the confirmatory assay to be run anyway as a model-monitoring control, so real-time release delivers information rather than cycle time.
modality_scope: monoclonal antibody, recombinant protein; extensible to cell and gene therapy
notes: SUB-AREA: bulk API/mAb

tech_name: Site-specific enzymatic and bioorthogonal ADC conjugation - ADC
principle: Attach the linker-payload at a defined engineered residue or enzymatically recognised motif rather than at stochastic lysines or reduced cysteines, producing a homogeneous drug-antibody ratio species so that purification is simpler, batch-to-batch variability falls and the therapeutic index is set by design rather than by an average.
trl_basis: Site-specific conjugation dominates filings and publications from 2020-2025 and is offered as a commercial CDMO capability, and manufacturing rather than science is described as the ADC bottleneck; operational demonstration with approved products still dominated by stochastic conjugation. [E-8028]
developers: Sutro Biopharma (non-canonical amino acids); Catalent/Lonza and other ADC CDMOs; Synaffix; Ambrx; Daiichi Sankyo and Seagen process groups
decisive_milestone: An approved ADC manufactured by site-specific enzymatic conjugation reports a commercial batch failure rate below 5 percent and cost of goods per gram at least 25 percent below a stochastic-conjugation comparator, disclosed in a peer-reviewed or regulatory-visible source; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Optimal conjugation site depends on the specific linker-payload, so there is no universal site and each pairing needs empirical optimisation; antibody engineering to install the site can perturb Fc function or manufacturability; and high-potency payload containment limits which facilities can run any of it.
commercialization_reasoning: The chemistry is commercially available now; the gate is that products designed with it must complete development, which is a five- to seven-year cycle from current pipeline positions.
failure_scenario: Homogeneity turns out not to be the driver of clinical outcome - stochastic ADCs with careful payload choice perform comparably - so the added antibody engineering cost buys manufacturing elegance and no clinical differentiation.
modality_scope: antibody-drug conjugates
notes: SUB-AREA: ADC conjugation Milestone quantified per X-25.

tech_name: Transferrin-receptor blood-brain-barrier shuttle biologics (Brainshuttle, transport vehicle)
principle: Fuse a moderate-affinity transferrin receptor binder to a therapeutic antibody or protein so that receptor-mediated transcytosis carries it across brain endothelium, raising brain exposure by roughly an order of magnitude and allowing a lower systemic dose for the same central effect.
trl_basis: CORRECTED under red-team finding X-24: the rating of 8 stands but the basis does not. Trontinemab's Phase 3 status supports 7 only. The formal decision that supports 8 is FDA's accelerated approval in March 2026 of tividenofusp alfa-eknm, an enzyme fused to a transferrin-receptor transport vehicle, for neurologic Hunter syndrome - an approved brain-shuttle biologic [E-8128]. Trontinemab's 91 percent amyloid PET negativity at 28 weeks [E-8016] remains supporting evidence for the platform, not the basis for the rating.
developers: Roche/Genentech (Brainshuttle); Denali Therapeutics (transport vehicle platform); Biogen; JCR Pharmaceuticals; academic BBB transport groups
decisive_milestone: A brain-shuttle-enabled therapeutic is approved with a label claim its unshuttled parent could not support; checkable by 2029 from the trontinemab Phase 3 readout and subsequent regulatory action.
remaining_hard_problems: Transferrin receptor is expressed on erythroid precursors, so affinity and valency must be tuned to avoid reticulocyte depletion; the shuttle raises brain exposure but does not control distribution within brain, so deep and white-matter regions may remain underdosed; and it works for proteins, not for the small molecules and oligonucleotides that many CNS targets require.
commercialization_reasoning: A Phase 3 programme is running now; approval on a positive readout would follow within roughly two years, making late-decade commercialisation the central case.
failure_scenario: The Phase 3 shows that raising brain exposure of an anti-amyloid antibody increases target engagement without a proportionate clinical benefit, which would indict the target rather than the shuttle - but would remove the commercial validation the platform needs.
modality_scope: antibodies, enzymes and protein therapeutics for CNS
notes: TRL basis corrected per X-24. Highest-TRL pure-P technology in the catalogue and now anchored on an approval rather than on trial stage.

tech_name: Machine-learning-designed AAV capsids for CNS, muscle and liver detargeting
principle: Generate and screen very large synthetic capsid libraries, train sequence-to-fitness models on the tropism and manufacturability data, and design capsids that cross the blood-brain barrier after intravenous dosing while detargeting liver, so that CNS gene therapy becomes systemic rather than intraparenchymal.
trl_basis: Preclinical data in non-human primates and humanised-receptor mice are reported by multiple developers with 50-75 percent brain transduction claims and an IND anticipated in 2026; validated in a relevant environment, with no clinical data. [E-8018][E-8019]
developers: Voyager Therapeutics (TRACER); Dyno Therapeutics; Broad Institute (Deverman laboratory); Caltech (Gradinaru laboratory); Novartis and Roche through partnerships
decisive_milestone: A first-in-human trial of an intravenously dosed ML-designed CNS capsid reports central target engagement at a tolerated systemic dose, with a published biomarker or biopsy readout; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Non-human primate tropism has repeatedly failed to predict human tropism for capsids, and the humanised-receptor mouse only tests one receptor hypothesis; pre-existing neutralising antibodies exclude a large fraction of patients regardless of capsid design; and systemic dosing at CNS-effective levels concentrates dose-limiting hepatotoxicity and complement activation risk.
commercialization_reasoning: IND filings are anticipated from 2026, so first-in-human data arrive in the late 2020s; a full clinical programme and approval adds five or more years.
failure_scenario: The human readout repeats the historical pattern: a capsid selected in primates transduces human brain far less efficiently, and the required systemic dose reproduces the hepatotoxicity and complement problems that limit existing AAV.
modality_scope: AAV gene therapy for CNS, muscle and eye
notes: depends on capsid fitness datasets (B10) and on manufacturability at the higher systemic doses (B6)

tech_name: Selective organ targeting lipid nanoparticles (SORT and successors)
principle: Add a fifth, charge-bearing lipid to the standard four-component LNP so that the protein corona formed in circulation directs the particle to lung, spleen or kidney rather than defaulting to hepatocytes, extending mRNA and siRNA therapeutics beyond the liver without a targeting ligand.
trl_basis: Robust rodent data with 60-80 percent knockdown after single intravenous dose and up to 88 percent lung protein downregulation, published in peer-reviewed literature; laboratory proof of concept with no clinical translation of the organ-targeting principle. [E-8050]
developers: UT Southwestern (Siegwart laboratory); ReCode Therapeutics; Ethris; academic LNP groups; several mRNA companies with internal programmes
decisive_milestone: A SORT-type organ-selective LNP demonstrates extrahepatic target-gene knockdown or protein expression in humans at a tolerated dose, with a tissue or biomarker readout; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: The mechanism depends on the protein corona, which differs between mouse and human plasma, so the organ selectivity may not transfer; repeat dosing of charged lipids raises immunogenicity and complement activation concerns that single-dose rodent studies do not surface; and selectivity is relative, not absolute, so liver exposure persists.
commercialization_reasoning: No clinical demonstration of the organ-selectivity principle exists, and LNP programmes take five to eight years from IND to approval, so a product depending on this mechanism is late in the next decade.
failure_scenario: Human protein corona differs enough that the selectivity collapses in first-in-human biodistribution imaging, and the field falls back to ligand-targeted particles.
modality_scope: mRNA, siRNA, gene editing payloads

tech_name: Antibody-targeted lipid nanoparticles for in vivo cell-type-specific delivery
principle: Decorate the LNP surface with a binder against a cell-surface marker such as CD8 or CD5, so that the particle is taken up preferentially by one lymphocyte subset and the mRNA payload is expressed only there, achieving cell-type specificity that lipid composition alone cannot deliver.
trl_basis: Lead candidates are in Phase 1 clinical evaluation and the leading developer was acquired by a large pharmaceutical company; demonstrated in a relevant clinical environment without efficacy readout. [E-8014][E-8089]
developers: Capstan Therapeutics (Eli Lilly); University of Pennsylvania (Weissman and June laboratories); Orna Therapeutics; several undisclosed pharma programmes
decisive_milestone: A clinical readout showing target-cell-restricted transgene expression in humans with quantified off-target uptake, published or presented with the biodistribution data; checkable by 2029.
remaining_hard_problems: Targeting ligands accelerate clearance by the mononuclear phagocyte system, so the fraction reaching target cells can be very small; the surface binder makes the particle an immunogen, limiting repeat dosing; and manufacturing a decorated LNP with consistent ligand density at commercial scale is unproven.
commercialization_reasoning: Phase 1 now; a first approval requires pivotal data and review, which is a four- to seven-year sequence from current stage.
failure_scenario: Anti-drug antibodies against the surface binder develop after the second or third dose, so the platform is confined to single-administration indications, which excludes most of the autoimmune uses it is being developed for.
modality_scope: mRNA and gene editing to immune cells; in vivo cell therapy
notes: enabling technology for in vivo CAR-T (T-030)

tech_name: MR-guided focused ultrasound blood-brain-barrier opening
principle: Inject circulating microbubbles and apply low-intensity focused ultrasound under MRI guidance to a chosen brain volume, so that oscillating bubbles transiently loosen tight junctions and any co-administered drug enters that region - making the barrier a controllable variable rather than a property of the molecule.
trl_basis: A sponsor-run Phase 1/2 in glioblastoma is published in Lancet Oncology, a Phase 2a in Alzheimer's disease is completed, and a randomised combination study appeared in NEJM; demonstrated in a relevant clinical environment, not yet approved for a drug-delivery indication. [E-8051][E-8052][E-8094]
developers: Insightec; Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre; West Virginia University Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute; Columbia University; Focused Ultrasound Foundation; University of Maryland and University of Virginia
decisive_milestone: A randomised trial shows that adding focused-ultrasound barrier opening to a systemically dosed drug improves a clinical endpoint, not just drug concentration or an imaging biomarker; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: The technique opens a treated volume, not the whole brain, so it suits focal disease and poorly suits diffuse neurodegeneration; each session requires MRI suite time and a trained team, which caps throughput at a level incompatible with chronic dosing; and long-term consequences of repeated barrier disruption, including inflammation and iron deposition, are uncharacterised.
commercialization_reasoning: Clinical programmes are running now; a combination indication requires a randomised efficacy trial of the combination, which is a five- to eight-year path including regulatory novelty of a device-drug combination claim.
failure_scenario: Increased drug concentration in the treated volume produces no clinical benefit because the limiting factor was target biology rather than exposure, and the procedure burden per session prevents adoption even where benefit exists.
modality_scope: any systemically administered CNS agent; device-drug combination

tech_name: Tumour-penetrating peptides and stromal modulation for solid-tumour access
principle: Use a peptide that binds integrin on tumour endothelium and is then proteolytically converted to a neuropilin-1 ligand, triggering an active bulk transport pathway that carries co-administered payload deep into tumour parenchyma against the interstitial pressure gradient that normally confines it to the perivascular rim.
trl_basis: Extensive preclinical demonstration across payload classes including oncolytic virus, bispecific engager and CAR-T co-administration; clinical translation of the penetration mechanism has not produced a positive controlled readout. [E-8053]
developers: Sanford Burnham Prebys (Ruoslahti laboratory); DrugCendR; academic CAR-T solid tumour groups; several oncology companies with internal programmes
decisive_milestone: A randomised trial shows that co-administering a tumour-penetrating peptide with an approved agent improves response rate over that agent alone in a solid tumour; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: The bulk transport pathway is heterogeneous across tumours and across regions of the same tumour, so the effect size is unpredictable per patient; the same pathway can enhance delivery to normal tissue expressing neuropilin-1; and the peptide's short half-life makes co-administration timing critical and hard to standardise.
commercialization_reasoning: Two decades of preclinical work have not yet produced a controlled clinical demonstration, which indicates a translational barrier rather than a development-timeline issue.
failure_scenario: The effect is real in mouse tumours with their characteristically leaky vasculature and disappears in human tumours with dense desmoplastic stroma - the tumours where penetration matters most.
modality_scope: oncology: small molecule, ADC, cell therapy, oncolytic virus

tech_name: Machine-learning immunogenicity prediction and computational deimmunisation
principle: Predict which peptides from a biologic will be presented on MHC class II and drive T-cell help for an anti-drug antibody response, then redesign the sequence to remove those epitopes while preserving folding and affinity, so that immunogenicity is engineered out before the molecule is made.
trl_basis: Commercial platforms are in routine industrial use with vendor-reported three-fold improvements in predicted-versus-observed ADA correlation, and a 2026 review documents the method class; demonstrated in a relevant environment, with predictive performance evidence controlled by the vendors. [E-8029]
developers: EpiVax (ISPRI, EpiSweep lineage); Lonza Applied Protein Services; Abzena; academic immunoinformatics groups; large biologics developers with internal tools
decisive_milestone: A prospective, blinded comparison across at least thirty clinical-stage biologics, published independently of the tool vendors, showing predicted ADA incidence tracks observed clinical ADA incidence; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Clinical immunogenicity depends on aggregation, formulation, impurities, route, dose interval and patient HLA distribution as much as on sequence, and none of these is captured by an epitope predictor. Innate immune signals and B-cell epitopes are largely unmodelled. Training labels come from assays whose cut-points differ between sponsors.
commercialization_reasoning: Already commercially deployed; the open question is independent validation, not availability.
failure_scenario: Deimmunised molecules still generate ADA at clinically relevant rates because aggregation and formulation dominate, and the field concludes that sequence-level prediction addresses a minority of the variance.
modality_scope: antibodies, enzymes, peptides, gene therapy transgene products

tech_name: Integrated in vitro plus in silico DILI battery (liver MPS, spheroids, toxicogenomics reference)
principle: Combine a human liver microphysiological readout, hepatocyte spheroid multi-parameter injury markers and a computational model trained on a large human toxicogenomics reference, so that hepatotoxicity is called on convergent human evidence rather than on any single assay whose sensitivity ceiling is known.
trl_basis: Component assays are individually validated with published performance, and a large-scale human toxicogenomics resource was published in Nature Communications; the integrated battery is validated in a relevant environment but has no agreed decision rule or qualified context of use. [E-8030][E-8086]
developers: FDA CDER; Emulate and CN Bio; academic toxicogenomics consortia; IQ Consortium MPS affiliate; European ToxRisk successors
decisive_milestone: A published prospective evaluation in which an integrated battery, with its decision rule fixed in advance, is applied to compounds entering first-in-human and its predictions are compared with subsequent clinical hepatotoxicity; checkable by 2031.
remaining_hard_problems: Idiosyncratic DILI is the clinically important form and is immune- and HLA-mediated, which none of the components model. Combining assays with correlated errors does not raise sensitivity as much as the independence assumption suggests, and there is no agreed weighting rule.
commercialization_reasoning: Individual components exist now; assembling and prospectively validating a battery with a fixed decision rule is a multi-year exercise that no single organisation currently owns.
failure_scenario: The battery raises sensitivity by flagging more compounds, and because the false-positive rate rises with it, programmes are killed that would have been safe - attrition moves earlier without improving late-stage success.
modality_scope: small molecule primarily

tech_name: Human iPSC cardiomyocyte assays coupled to in silico proarrhythmia modelling
