trl_basis: Operating in the real environment: BF-BOIN is published in Clinical Cancer Research with formal cohort-opening rules and a seamless two-stage Phase I/II design with backfill appeared in Pharmaceutical Statistics in 2026 [E-8119], and Bayesian dose-finding adoption reached 75 percent of surveyed early-phase oncology protocols in 2024 [E-8109]. Not 8 because no guidance or qualification specifies any particular design.
developers: MD Anderson (Yuan and Ji groups, trialdesign.org); Takeda and other industry biostatistics groups; academic Bayesian adaptive design methodologists; FDA Office of Biostatistics through review precedent
decisive_milestone: At least 10 registrational oncology programmes report that the registrational dose was selected from a within-trial randomised comparison embedded in a seamless Phase I/II design, disclosed in the approval package or a peer-reviewed publication; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Randomised dose comparison inside an early-phase trial is powered for a utility contrast, not for survival, so it can select confidently on the wrong quantity. Backfill cohorts enrol at doses whose safety is still being established, which shifts risk onto patients enrolled before the escalation completes. Joint efficacy-toxicity utility functions require a weighting that no one can specify from data, so the answer partly encodes the sponsor's prior preference.
commercialization_reasoning: The designs are published and in operational use now; the window closes as the first programmes designed this way reach registration.
failure_scenario: The backfill machinery is adopted for its schedule benefit and the randomised dose comparison is not, so trials get faster and the dose is still chosen from a non-randomised cross-cohort look - the exact failure this bottleneck describes.
modality_scope: oncology small molecule, ADC, bispecific; extensible to any dose-limited modality
notes: WATCH FLAG: backfill's headline benefit is speed. Only the randomised dose-comparison component attacks P; a sponsor that adopts backfill without randomisation makes a bad design faster and should not be counted as relieving B17

tech_name: Estimand framework (ICH E9(R1)) as enforced endpoint and population specification
principle: Require that the quantity being estimated be written down before the trial - population, treatment, endpoint, summary measure, and how each intercurrent event such as discontinuation or rescue therapy is handled - so that the clinical question and the statistical analysis cannot silently diverge, and so that a positive result cannot be produced by an analysis convention chosen after the data arrive.
trl_basis: A formal decision in force across jurisdictions: regulators in the EU, US, Canada, Singapore, China, Switzerland and Chinese Taipei require estimands in submissions, with Taiwan adopting on 15 April 2026 and Brazil, Korea and Japan implementing [E-8116]. Not 9 because compliance quality is uneven and there is no published evaluation of whether specification changed conclusions.
developers: ICH E9(R1) expert working group; FDA and EMA biostatistics offices; national regulators adopting the addendum; industry statistical leadership through PSI and ASA working groups
decisive_milestone: A published empirical evaluation of at least 100 pivotal trials submitted before and after E9(R1) shows a fall of at least 30 percent in the rate of post hoc changes to the primary analysis population or estimand between protocol and submission; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Specifying an estimand does not tell you which estimand is clinically right, and the framework is neutral between a treatment-policy and a hypothetical strategy that can give materially different answers on the same data. Intercurrent events that matter most - discontinuation for toxicity - are the ones whose handling is most contested and least standardised across therapeutic areas.
commercialization_reasoning: The addendum has been in force in major markets since 2019-2021 and adoption completed across most ICH members by 2026; the window closes as the remaining implementers finish.
failure_scenario: Estimand sections become boilerplate copied between protocols, specifying the convention the sponsor was going to use anyway, so the framework documents rather than disciplines the endpoint choice.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: Attacks the endpoint-definition component of B17 rather than dose

tech_name: Predictive enrichment and adaptive population-enrichment designs
principle: Define the trial population by a prospectively specified marker of likely response, or start broad and use a prespecified interim rule to restrict later accrual to the subgroup where the treatment effect is concentrating, so that the trial answers the question of whether the drug works in the population it works in rather than diluting a real effect across a population half of which cannot respond.
trl_basis: Operating in the real environment: FDA's enrichment guidance has been final since March 2019 [E-8117] and biomarker-defined registrational trials are routine in oncology, while adaptive enrichment with an interim population-restriction rule remains uncommon. Not 8 because no formal decision establishes adaptive enrichment as an accepted registrational design class.
developers: FDA CDER and the Oncology Center of Excellence; Cytel and Berry Consultants; academic adaptive-design biostatisticians; sponsors running biomarker-stratified registrational programmes
decisive_milestone: At least 5 approvals are granted where the labelled population was narrowed by a prespecified interim enrichment rule executed inside the pivotal trial, rather than defined before the trial began; checkable by 2031 from approval review documents.
remaining_hard_problems: The enrichment marker must be measurable, prespecified and biologically right before the trial, and if the marker is wrong the design enriches confidently for the wrong subgroup. Interim subgroup selection inflates type I error unless the multiplicity is handled, and the correction costs much of the efficiency gain. Narrowing the population narrows the market, which sets the design against the commercial case.
commercialization_reasoning: Prespecified enrichment is standard now; adaptive interim enrichment requires regulatory precedent that accumulates one approval at a time, which puts routine acceptance around the turn of the decade.
failure_scenario: Enrichment is used to rescue an underpowered trial by selecting the subgroup that happens to be ahead at interim, the result does not replicate, and regulators tighten the multiplicity requirement to the point where the design loses its advantage.
modality_scope: oncology, immunology, neurology; all modalities

tech_name: Patient-reported tolerability as an input to dose selection (PRO-CTCAE, core PRO guidance)
principle: Measure symptomatic adverse events directly from the patient at each dose, and put that measurement into the exposure-response analysis alongside clinician-graded toxicity, so that the dose is chosen against the burden that actually drives discontinuation in practice rather than against a clinician-graded scale that systematically under-records symptom severity.
trl_basis: Accepted into a regulatory pathway and no further: FDA's 2023 draft core patient-reported outcomes guidance supports self-reported symptomatic adverse events in early-phase dose optimisation, PRO-CTCAE is an established instrument, and PRO exposure-response analysis for dose optimisation was a named FDA fellowship topic for 2026 [E-8118]. No guidance is final and no labelled dose has been set on this basis.
developers: National Cancer Institute (PRO-CTCAE); FDA Oncology Center of Excellence; ISOQOL; academic patient-centred outcomes groups; sponsors piloting PRO in Phase 1
decisive_milestone: At least 3 registrational programmes disclose that the selected dose was changed by patient-reported tolerability data, with the PRO exposure-response analysis described in the approval package; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: PRO completion falls precisely in the patients who are sickest, so the tolerability signal is missing where it matters most and the missingness is informative. There is no agreed threshold that converts a symptom-burden score into a dose decision, and cross-trial comparability of PRO-CTCAE summary scores is not established.
commercialization_reasoning: The instrument exists and the draft guidance supports the use; converting a symptom score into a defensible dose decision needs a scoring and threshold convention that the methodological literature says is unresolved.
failure_scenario: PRO data are collected because the guidance asks for them, reported descriptively, and never enter the exposure-response analysis, so tolerability remains a narrative appended to a dose chosen on clinician-graded toxicity.
modality_scope: oncology first; extensible to any chronically dosed therapy

tech_name: Eligibility-criteria modernisation as population definition (ASCO-Friends recommendations, FDA 2024 draft guidances)
principle: Remove exclusion criteria that were copied forward without a safety rationale - brain metastases, prior malignancy, borderline organ function, performance status 2 - so that the trial population is defined by the biology the drug addresses rather than by inherited convention, and so that the answer the trial gives applies to the patients who will actually receive the drug.
trl_basis: Operating in the real environment: FDA issued three draft cancer eligibility guidances on 26 April 2024 incorporating ASCO-Friends working group recommendations, and applying three broadened criteria roughly doubled the potentially eligible lung cancer population in a real-world database [E-8120]. Not 8 because the guidances are draft.
developers: ASCO and Friends of Cancer Research joint working groups; FDA Oncology Center of Excellence; CancerLinQ and real-world data holders; NCI cooperative groups
decisive_milestone: The proportion of new registrational oncology protocols that exclude patients with treated stable brain metastases falls below 25 percent, against the historical majority; checkable by 2029 from a protocol audit of ClinicalTrials.gov records.
remaining_hard_problems: Broadening eligibility is not unambiguously good for the estimate: adding patients with lower expected benefit dilutes the average treatment effect and can convert a real subgroup effect into a null overall result. There is no accepted method for deciding which criteria are inherited convention and which are protecting a real safety signal, and the decision is currently made by consensus rather than by data.
commercialization_reasoning: Draft guidances are out and adoption in protocols is measurable now; finalisation and protocol turnover complete within a few years.
failure_scenario: Eligibility is broadened, the treatment effect is diluted, the trial reads out negative, and the field concludes - wrongly - that the drug does not work rather than that the population was mis-specified.
modality_scope: oncology first; principle applies to all therapeutic areas
notes: AMBIGUOUS SIGN: the primary effect is accrual (T and C), and the P effect can be negative through dilution. Counted under B17 because it is a population-definition decision, not an operational one; also relevant to B3

tech_name: Target trial emulation for population and comparator definition
principle: Before running a trial, write the protocol of the hypothetical randomised trial you wish you could run, then emulate it in observational data to see what the eligibility criteria, comparator and follow-up window imply about event rates, competing risks and effect size - so that the population and comparator in the real trial are chosen against an empirical estimate rather than against an assumption.
trl_basis: Validated in a relevant environment: the framework is established in the methodological literature and a 2026 npj Digital Medicine paper supplies an operational specification separating trial design from its realisation in electronic health record data, including conditions under which the estimate is uninterpretable [E-8121]. Used to inform design, not yet an accepted basis for a design decision in a submission.
developers: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (Hernan group); FDA and EMA real-world evidence programmes; Aetion and RWE analytics vendors; academic pharmacoepidemiology groups
decisive_milestone: At least 5 pivotal trial protocols cite a target trial emulation as the stated basis for the choice of eligibility criteria or comparator, in the protocol or the regulatory briefing package; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: The method improves the design of an observational analysis; it does not remove unmeasured confounding, measurement error or incomplete follow-up, and its output is only as good as whether the electronic health record can express the trial's design components at all - which the 2026 framework says it often cannot.
commercialization_reasoning: The methodology is mature and the operational framework is new; adoption as a design input rather than as an evidence-generation method depends on sponsors building the capability, which runs a few years.
failure_scenario: The emulation reproduces the confounding that made the observational estimate wrong in the first place, the real trial is designed against it, and the design error is now quantitatively justified rather than merely assumed.
modality_scope: all modalities; strongest where a large routine-care population exists

tech_name: Trial-design simulation with prespecified operating characteristics (OCTAVE-class frameworks)
principle: Simulate the proposed design thousands of times against explicitly stated data-generating assumptions before enrolling anyone, and report type I error, power, bias, precision and interim-decision probabilities across the plausible range - so that a design is chosen on its measured behaviour under uncertainty rather than on a single power calculation at one assumed effect size.
trl_basis: Demonstrated in a relevant environment: simulation is required to characterise complex adaptive and platform designs, a 2026 Statistics in Medicine paper sets the OCTAVE framework for planning and validating such studies, and Nature Reviews Drug Discovery published a 2026 review of simulation-guided design [E-8122]. Standards are new and not yet a submission requirement.
developers: Academic biostatistics groups publishing OCTAVE; Berry Consultants and Cytel; EU-PEARL platform simulation working group; FDA Office of Biostatistics; open-source multi-arm multi-stage design software maintainers
decisive_milestone: A regulator requires a prespecified simulation report with stated data-generating mechanisms as part of the protocol package for complex adaptive designs, or at least 20 pivotal protocols publish one; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: Operating characteristics are only valid under the assumed data-generating mechanism, and the assumption most likely to be wrong - the treatment effect and its heterogeneity - is the one the simulation cannot check. Simulation optimises the statistical properties of a design and is silent on whether the scientific question is the right one.
commercialization_reasoning: The framework papers are from 2026; standardisation of simulation reporting across sponsors and regulators typically runs three to five years from a methods standard to expectation.
failure_scenario: Simulation is used to find the design with the best operating characteristics for a trial asking the wrong question at the wrong dose in the wrong population, producing a rigorously characterised failure.
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: WATCH FLAG: this is the clearest instance in B17 of a technology that can make a bad design more efficient. Value is conditional on T-082, T-086 and T-087 fixing the design content first

tech_name: Proteome-wide cis-pQTL Mendelian randomisation
principle: Use a genetic variant sitting at the gene encoding a specific protein, which raises or lowers that protein's circulating level from birth, as an instrumental variable for pharmacologically modulating that protein - giving a randomised natural experiment in humans, run for a lifetime, testing the causal direction between the target and the disease without a clinical trial. Colocalisation is applied as a filter to exclude variants tagging a neighbouring gene.
trl_basis: Demonstrated in a relevant environment at industrial scale: the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project measured about 2,923 proteins with genome-wide association analyses in 50,395 participants [E-8124], and proteome-wide MR screens are now routine across respiratory, cardiovascular, psychiatric, haematological and oncology indications [E-8125]. Held at 6 and no higher because the one published test of predictive performance found that MR significance alone did not enrich for Phase II success while GWAS support did [E-8009].
developers: UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project consortium (13 pharmaceutical companies with UK Biobank); deCODE genetics; Olink and SomaLogic as assay platforms; MRC Integrative Epidemiology Unit Bristol; Open Targets
decisive_milestone: A prospective, pre-registered analysis reports that targets selected by cis-pQTL MR with colocalisation have a Phase II success rate at least 1.5-fold that of matched non-MR-supported targets, on a cohort of at least 200 target-indication pairs entered after 2024; checkable by 2032.
remaining_hard_problems: A lifelong small shift in a protein's level is not the same perturbation as a large acute pharmacological block, so direction can be right and magnitude and reversibility wrong. Affinity-based proteomic assays measure epitope availability rather than protein concentration, and a cis-variant that alters the epitope produces a spurious pQTL. Plasma protein level is a poor proxy for tissue-level activity for most targets. Above all, the only published outcome test returned negative for MR specifically.
commercialization_reasoning: The resource base industrialised with the 2023 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project release and screens are already routine; what is missing is not availability but a demonstration that the instrument predicts clinical outcome, which requires a cohort of MR-selected targets to complete Phase II.
failure_scenario: The instrument continues to generate large numbers of statistically significant, biologically plausible and clinically unproductive target nominations, because circulating protein level is causally upstream of nothing that a drug can usefully change in the relevant tissue - and the negative Phase II enrichment result already on record is the first sign of exactly this.
modality_scope: all modalities; restricted to targets that are secreted or shed into plasma and have a cis-pQTL
notes: ADDED under red-team finding X-26. Distinct from T-002: T-002 is GWAS-and-colocalisation-based target selection, this is the protein-instrument variant. It is a causal human instrument that does not require a trial, which corrects the over-strong sentence in the original B1 negative claim; it is not yet a solution to B1 because the objection to it is empirical

tech_name: Delinked subscription payment for antimicrobials (NHS Antimicrobial Products Subscription Model)
principle: Pay a fixed annual fee for access to an antimicrobial, set by an assessment of its value to the health system and explicitly detached from the volume dispensed, so that a product whose correct clinical use is to be held in reserve still earns a return. This directly inverts the market failure in which stewardship destroys the revenue that funds development.
trl_basis: A formal decision in force and procuring: pilot contracts were awarded in July 2022 to Pfizer and Shionogi, the model was scaled in the May 2024 UK antimicrobial resistance action plan, NHS tendered contracts in August 2024 at an estimated GBP 1.9 billion over 16 years covering all four UK nations with an annual budget near GBP 100 million, and those contracts were set to begin on 1 April 2026 [E-8126]. Not 9 because it operates in one country and no effect on the development pipeline has been measured.
developers: NHS England and NICE; UK Department of Health and Social Care; devolved administrations of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; Pfizer and Shionogi as pilot contract holders; US PASTEUR Act proponents as the analogous instrument
decisive_milestone: The number of antibacterial candidates entering Phase 1 from companies holding or eligible for subscription contracts rises above its 2019-2023 baseline, and at least one additional G7 payer executes a delinked subscription contract; checkable by 2030.
remaining_hard_problems: One national payer at GBP 100 million per year is far below the global revenue an antibiotic developer would need to justify a programme, so the instrument corrects the sign of the incentive without correcting its magnitude. Setting the fixed fee requires valuing a product whose benefit is mostly option value against a future resistance state that has not occurred, and no accepted method for that valuation exists. The model is renewable by government and therefore exposed to fiscal cycles shorter than a development programme.
commercialization_reasoning: Piloted 2022, tendered 2024, contracts commencing April 2026; whether other payers follow, and whether pipeline entry responds, resolves within roughly five years of the first full contracts.
failure_scenario: The subscription revenue proves too small to change investment decisions, antibiotic developers continue to fail commercially after approval, and the model is judged a success on access metrics while the pipeline it was meant to refill stays empty.
modality_scope: antibacterials and antifungals; the delinkage principle extends to any low-volume high-option-value product
notes: ADDED under red-team finding X-27. More mature than the generic advance-market-commitment entry T-062, which describes the same mechanism class in its proposal form; T-062 should be read as superseded for antimicrobials

tech_name: Just-in-time site activation with master clinical trial agreements and single-IRB reliance
principle: Pre-negotiate the contract, budget and ethics reliance with a site before any specific protocol exists, so that when a protocol is approved the site is activated by executing a short work order instead of a fresh agreement - converting a serial legal negotiation that runs months into a step measured in days, and letting sites be activated only when a candidate patient appears rather than speculatively.
trl_basis: Operating in the real environment with measured benchmarks: average clinical trial agreement execution runs 45 days at central-IRB sites and 145 days at local-IRB sites, and just-in-time programmes using master agreements are reported to cut these to 14 and 30 days [E-8129]. Not 8 because no formal requirement or standard mandates the approach and adoption is sponsor-by-sponsor.
developers: Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development as benchmark source; WCG and central IRBs; large CROs operating just-in-time activation programmes; NIH single-IRB policy under the revised Common Rule; academic medical centre contracting offices
decisive_milestone: A sponsor or CRO reports median clinical trial agreement execution below 30 days at local-IRB sites across a portfolio of at least 50 sites, against the 145-day benchmark, together with median time from protocol final to first patient in below 90 days; checkable by 2029 [E-8129].
remaining_hard_problems: Master agreements move the negotiation earlier rather than removing it, and the contentious terms - indemnity, intellectual property, publication rights, injury compensation - are the ones institutions will not pre-agree in the abstract. Just-in-time activation also transfers idle-capacity risk to the site, which sites with the least slack are least able to absorb.
commercialization_reasoning: The approach is in commercial operation now; the window covers the period for master-agreement coverage to reach the majority of a typical trial's site list, which is limited by institution-by-institution negotiation rather than by any technical step.
failure_scenario: Startup time falls and enrollment does not, because activation speed was not the binding constraint: patients are lost upstream of screening at 59 percent of sites [E-8091] and the trained coordinators needed to run an activated site remain scarce [E-8039].
modality_scope: all modalities
notes: REPLACES T-017, removed per X-24 as a labour-capacity constraint rather than a technology. Milestone quantified per X-25. B3 elasticity is 0.6 in the current matrix, so this is a low-value entry even though it works
